chunks: And Asim ibn Humayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

There was a man in the time of Ali (peace be upon him) who had two female slaves. They both gave birth in one night, one gave birth to a son and the other to a daughter. The owner of the daughter took her daughter and placed her in the cradle with the son, and took her son, saying, 'The son is mine.' The owner of the son said, 'The son is mine.' So they referred their dispute to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him). He ordered that their milk be weighed and said, 'Whichever had heavier milk, the son belongs to her.'
So they went to him and recounted the story to him. He (peace be upon him) said, 'As for this, if one of them killed a man, the other has given life. And Allah says,
ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali resolve the dispute between two women claiming the same child?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s (AS) use of empirical evidence (weighing milk) to resolve a complex custody dispute, demonstrating the practical application of *bayyinah* (proof) in Shia jurisprudence. The text further elucidates the legal principle of *tadakhul* (overlap) of rights, where the surviving child’s life serves as compensation for the mother’s death, with the *diyah* drawn from the *Bayt al-Mal* rather than the child’s estate, reflecting the Imam’s nuanced approach to justice and public welfare.
